notes.1a: Nearly all candidates were able to record a correct reading from the thermometer.
notes.1b: Most candidates correctly identified the units, but some failed to give any response.
notes.1c: Many candidates gained full credit, but some made incorrect reference to the heater. This is an example where careful reading of a question was needed.
notes.1d: Many candidates only gained partial credit as they made no reference to values from the results.
notes.1ei: (iii) Most candidates successfully carried out both calculations but a few failed to give the correct unit.
notes.1fi: Many candidates gave imprecise answers with confusing responses about which beaker they were referring to. Several candidates described repeating the experiment with a lid. Again, this was an example where careful reading of the question was needed.
notes.1fii: Most candidates gained partial credit for stating that the starting temperature must be the same with many gaining full credit for correctly explaining that the cooling rate was different at different temperatures.
notes.2a: Many candidates correctly inserted the ammeter in series with the rest of the circuit but fewer connected the voltmeter across the terminals XY correctly. Some candidates also left a gap in the circuit.
notes.2bi: Nearly all candidates correctly read both meters, with only a very few incorrectly reading the ammeter as 0.26.
notes.2bii: Most candidates correctly calculated the values of R but inconsistent significant figures were often seen.
notes.2biii: Most candidates correctly completed the headings in the table .
notes.2ci: Most candidates correctly calculated the values of P and Q
notes.2cii: There were many correct statements with the justification of being within the limits of experimental accuracy frequently seen.
notes.2d: Only stronger candidates answered this correctly.
notes.3a: Most candidates correctly measured the height of the object.
notes.3b: Many candidates gained credit, but some referred to moving the lens rather than moving the screen back and forth which gained no credit.
notes.3c: Most candidates correctly completed the table.
notes.3d: Nearly all candidates attempted the graph with most labelling the axes correctly and using suitable scales. Candidates should not assume that a graph must start from the origin unless specifically instructed to do so. The plotting of points was generally very good, but some candidates’ points were too large. They should be no larger than half a small square on the graph. There were many good lines of best fit with an even distribution of points on either side if necessary. Lines should not automatically be extended to the origin.
notes.3ei: Many candidates correctly drew the triangle on the graph to identify how they would calculate the gradient.
notes.3eii: Many candidates correctly calculated the focal length, but some were out of range.
notes.3f: The most common correct answers for a difficulty were either putting something (e.g. a ruler) in the way of the light or the image having blurred edges. Using a larger object or marking the image on the screen were the most common improvements to make.
